summary: In this story, when their school bus breaks down far from the village, two classmates decide to walk the familiar road home together, helping each other and meeting a kind farmer along the way.
introduce: Show the title “The Long Walk Home” and ask, “What do you think will happen in this story, and why?” Explain that good readers use clues in the text together with what they already know to make inferences.

keyTerms.def: the path or way a person travels from one place to another

challengeTerms.def: a friendly and generous welcome given to guests or strangers
steady effort to keep trying despite difficulty

discussion: Do you agree or disagree that it is better to wait for help than to walk home on your own? Use evidence from the story to explain.
Explain how Hind and Sara worked together to get home safely.
struggling: Read the first part of the story aloud together, review route, exhausted, and grateful, and let weak readers answer “What clue tells you that?” questions using sentence starters.
gifted: Challenge advanced readers to use parched, hospitality, and perseverance in a short paragraph that makes an inference that the story does not state and support it with two clues.
